City-traffic-M: congestion and volume on 18 October 2024

The saved city-traffic-M visualization contains 720 roads on 2024-10-18. Its 96 fifteen-minute frames cover the day from 00:00 to 24:00; the last frame starts at 23:45. The default maps show 13:30, the original peak-congestion selection. The two trends cover all saved frames.

Source and data preparation

The metadata identifies mightyneghbor/city-traffic-benchmarks, version 4. Upstream files are city-traffic-M-raw-static-features.parquet, city-traffic-M-raw-volume.parquet and city-traffic-M-raw-speed.parquet. The saved map consists of city_traffic_M_osm_congestion_sample.html and its companion JS and JSON files.

Data preparation validates the JSON literal assigned to window.CITY_TRAFFIC_OSM_SAMPLE, then wraps its original text in the reporting schema. The segment order, geometry, frame metrics and aggregate summaries are preserved. The companion JSON contains the same payload.

source_js <- 'city_traffic_M_osm_congestion_sample.js'
source_lines <- readLines(source_js, warn=FALSE, encoding='UTF-8')
pattern <- '^\\s*window\\.CITY_TRAFFIC_OSM_SAMPLE\\s*=\\s*'
payload <- sub(';\\s*$', '', sub(pattern, '',
               grep(pattern, source_lines, value=TRUE)))
stopifnot(length(payload)==1L, jsonlite::validate(payload))
provenance <- jsonlite::toJSON(list(
  source_html=sub('\\.js$','.html',basename(source_js)),
  source_js=basename(source_js), source_md5=unname(tools::md5sum(source_js))),
  auto_unbox=TRUE)
artifact <- paste0('{"schema_version":1,"source":"metropolis","provenance":',
                   provenance,',"payload":{"data":',payload,'}}')
output_file <- 'data/metropolis-real.json.gz'
stopifnot(!file.exists(output_file))
dir.create(dirname(output_file), recursive=TRUE, showWarnings=FALSE)
con <- gzfile(output_file, 'wt')
tryCatch(writeLines(artifact, con, useBytes=TRUE), finally=close(con))

Preparation is separate from rendering. The report reads the saved file data/metropolis-real.json.gz.

The bundled bdynets_0.1.0.tar.gz supplies the version 0.1.0 source package, including its license. The report setup and run.R use an installed package when available; otherwise they install the bundled source into a temporary library for that R session. The package depends on magrittr in addition to standard R libraries. R Markdown rendering uses jsonlite, rmarkdown, knitr and Pandoc. The preparation code creates its output directory and refuses to overwrite an existing dataset.

The original generator, build_city_traffic_osm_congestion_sample.py, performs the following processing:

Stage Saved construction
Road selection Selects 720 roads with nonzero volume using volume ranking and a 34 by 22 spatial grid.
Day selection Selects the highest-volume eligible day with at least 288 five-minute records.
Temporal aggregation Averages three five-minute observations into each fifteen-minute frame, interpolates in both directions, then fills remaining missing values with zero.
Speed reference Uses each road’s whole-period 90th percentile of nonzero speed.
Payload Saves road arrays, display scales and frame summaries; speed and volume have two decimal places and congestion three.

Saved fields

x <- read_traffic_data(params$dataset)
meta <- x$data$metadata
stopifnot(x$source=='metropolis', !isTRUE(meta$synthetic),
          meta$sampleDay=='2024-10-18', length(x$data$frames)==96L,
          meta$frameIntervalMinutes==15L,
          x$data$frames[[1]]$time=='2024-10-18 00:00',
          x$data$frames[[96]]$time=='2024-10-18 23:45')
knitr::kable(data.frame(roads=length(x$data$segments), frames=length(x$data$frames),
                       minutes_per_frame=meta$frameIntervalMinutes))
roads frames minutes_per_frame
720 96 15
Field Definition
segments Road IDs, endpoint coordinates, static attributes, speed reference and maximum volume.
frames[].volume, speed Saved road-level fifteen-minute averages.
frames[].congestion Descriptive road-level index between zero and one.
congestionMean, meanVolume Saved means for the whole frame.
meanSpeed, active Mean speed over positive-volume roads, and the number of those roads.
metadata Source, day, aggregation rule, display scale and peak frame.

The saved metadata does not establish the formal measurement units, timezone or CRS. The source viewer labels speed as km/h. Interpreting saved x and y as longitude and latitude places the roads near Yekaterinburg; the metadata does not supply a publisher-confirmed city name.

Maps and daily trends

figures <- traffic_osm_figures(params$dataset, 'metropolis',
                          time_index=params$time_index)

R frame 55 corresponds to JavaScript frame 54 and 13:30. The source selects this frame by total congestion. The congestion map uses the saved index; the volume map divides volume by the saved daily 95th percentile, 69.33, and clips the display scale to one. Both use a green, amber and red palette, with different quantities behind their colors. Static widths follow the source scaling and dark road casings.

The source congestion index combines nonnegative slowdown and a clipped log-volume weight:

congestion = clip(1 - speed / road_p90_speed, 0, 1)
             * clip(log1p(volume) / log1p(day_volume_p95), 0, 1)

The generator handles nonfinite intermediate values before saving. The report reads the saved congestion array rather than recomputing it from rounded speed and volume. Daily trends also read saved congestionMean and meanVolume summaries. The dashed line marks the selected frame.

Geometry uses Web Mercator for display. OSM supplies the original viewer’s background context; it does not enter the congestion calculation or establish network adjacency. These static panels contain the saved data layers over cached OSM-derived roads and water.

Selected-frame statistics

selected_frame <- x$data$frames[[params$time_index]]
statistics <- unlist(selected_frame[c('congestionMean','congestionP95',
                                     'meanSpeed','meanVolume','active')])
knitr::kable(data.frame(statistic=names(statistics), value=unname(statistics)))
statistic value
congestionMean 0.206
congestionP95 0.766
meanSpeed 49.340
meanVolume 35.260
active 632.000

The selected frame starts at 2024-10-18 13:30. congestionMean and congestionP95 summarize the saved road congestion index. meanVolume is the saved mean across all selected roads; meanSpeed is the saved mean over roads with positive volume. active counts those positive-volume roads. These values come from the original frame summary rather than a recalculation from rounded road arrays. The displayed means are 0.206 for congestion, 35.26 for volume and 49.34 for speed, with 632 active roads.

Offline geographic context

osm-figures.R draws the saved traffic frames over data/osm-basemap.json.gz. download_osm.py records the cache preparation: zoom-11 roads, water and places layers from the Protomaps archive dated 20 October 2026, covering the saved map bounds with a 0.02-degree margin. The cache contains the source URL, retrieval time, individual tile hashes and a checksum of the extracted geometry. Preparation depends on Python packages requests, pmtiles and mapbox-vector-tile; rendering reads the local cache without network requests.

The background is a generalized contemporary OSM extract. It supplies spatial context without changing traffic geometry, values, colors or connectivity. Available English place labels are thinned for readability. The basemap is not a reconstruction of the road network on the traffic observation date. Map data: OpenStreetMap contributors, via Protomaps, ODbL Produced Work.

Frame selection and export

The time_index parameter covers R indices 1 through 96. Frame 33 starts at 08:00. The plotting workflow also provides individual maps, trends and exports:

plot_traffic_osm(traffic_frame(x, time_index=33L, metric='volume'),
                 read_osm_basemap())
plot(traffic_trend(x, metric='congestion', time_index=33L))
traffic_osm_figures(params$dataset, 'metropolis', time_index=33L,
                output_dir='output/metropolis-0800')

Exports contain four PDF and PNG figures and source records. The HTML embeds all four panels. Dependencies are bdynets, jsonlite, rmarkdown and knitr, with Pandoc for HTML conversion.

Interpretation

Volume ranking and spatial thinning determine the displayed roads, so the trends describe this selected set. Interpolation and zero filling conceal raw missingness. The whole-period speed reference includes observations outside the displayed day and can leak future information into prediction. Individual vehicle paths and validated directed adjacency are absent from this payload. Congestion-source attribution depends on those additional data and an explicit analysis model.
